summary: Initial POC scoping between Redwood and Pictor Financial to define workload characterization and success criteria for a pilot focused on customer-facing recommendation and compliance summarization features. Main goals: establish QPS/concurrency baseline, token distribution (input/output), benchmark matrix, data access and security requirements, and timeline for a 3-week POC.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-07-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (SE), Liam Chen (Product) -- Aisha Khan (CTO, Pictor), Markus Lee (Platform Eng), Dana Ortiz (Product), Evan Gupta (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Discussed traffic shape, token mixes, burst patterns; decided to run two benchmark passes: representative QPS and high-concurrency stress. Pictor to provide logs and sample prompts; Redwood to provide test harness and benchmark plan.

[00:00] Jordan (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 40 minutes, goal for today is to lock down the POC scope and the measurable success criteria, and then next steps for data sharing.
[00:20] Aisha (CTO): thanks Jordan, appreciate it. We want to make sure the pilot mirrors our production traffic shape — lots of short prompts for recommendations and some longer compliance summarizations. Latency is important for recommendations, cost is important overall.
[00:35] Samira (SE): got it. can you ballpark QPS during peak windows and typical concurrency, and also what's the token mix? that helps pick model variants and batching configs.
[00:48] Markus (Platform Eng): sure, our peak recommendation QPS is about 120 rps sustained for 10 minutes during business hours, with spikes up to 350 rps for 30s from promotions. Concurrency per model instance is roughly 60 at baseline. For the summarization flow, it's lower QPS, like 2-4 qps, but each call is longer - input ~1k tokens and output ~800 tokens.
[01:20] Jordan: nice. so two distinct shapes: high QPS low-token and low QPS high-token. how much of total traffic is recommendations vs summarize?
[01:33] Dana (Product): around 82% recommendations, 14% summarizations, 4% other helper calls. Recommendations median tokens in/out are pretty small, median input ~28 tokens, output ~15 tokens. There's also a tail of ~10% longer prompts for multi-step flows.
[01:55] Samira: the token distribution matters for batching and KV cache behaviour; also quantization tradeoffs change on long sequences. did you say KV cache? sometimes transcripts say KV cash but it's KV cache.
[02:10] Markus: right, KV cache — we pin the prompt context for session-based recs. cache hit rate around 42% today.
[02:20] Liam (Redwood Product): are these sessions sticky to a user or ephemeral? sticky would benefit from prefix caching.
[02:28] Aisha: yes sticky to user session for about 15 minutes; for recommendations we do prefix match for the user's profile.
[02:40] Samira: good. for the pilot we'll model a 24-hour representative window and a separate stress window to capture those promotion spikes. proposed baseline QPS for pilot: 125 rps sustained for 15m, spike window: 400 rps for 60s. thoughts?
[02:58] Markus: 125 sustained is fine. the 400 spike is conservative but realistic. how do you plan to simulate the session stickiness?
[03:08] Samira: we'll use the session id distribution you provide in the traffic export and replay at the same ratio. if that's not available we'll approximate with a Zipf distribution across users.
[03:20] Aisha: we'll include session ids, hashed; can you confirm you do not need PII?
[03:27] Jordan: yes we only need hashed ids + prompt text; we recommend you scrub any raw PII before sharing, but we can work with hashed identifiers.
[03:35] Evan (Security): on data sharing, critical for us to understand encryption at rest and KMS integration, plus audit logs. Is Redwood Private an option or would you prefer Dedicated?
[03:48] Samira: technically both are possible. for a short 3-week POC most customers start with Hosted but with private networking options; if you have strict compliance we can do a private deployment in your VPC or on-prem. For the benchmark itself we can often run in Redwood Dedicated and ensure isolation.
[04:05] Evan: we need KMS and HSM support, and SOC2 attestation. also retention controls for logs.
[04:14] Jordan: we'll share the compliance pack and SOC2 report after this call. Samira will add the KMS/HSM matrix to the action items.
[04:22] Samira: noted.
[04:28] [05:00] Jordan: let's sketch success criteria — what needs to pass for you to consider the POC successful?
[05:08] Dana: primary: recommendation latency p95 < 350ms under baseline traffic, and p50 < 120ms. For summarization throughput we want processing latency p95 < 2.2s and quality parity within 3% of our current on-prem baseline according to our eval prompts. Cost target is 25% or better vs current CPU-based infra for the same SLA.
[05:36] Samira: the quality parity is important — can you share eval prompt sets and the metric you use? precision/recall or human-in-the-loop scoring?
[05:45] Dana: it's a mix — we have automated checks for hallucination rate and a human rating sample for relevance. we'll share a 200-prompt eval set and the scoring rubric.
[05:58] [06:20] Markus: operationally, we need token-level billing estimates per 100k requests and an expected monthly run-rate for cost modeling.
[06:30] Liam: we will include token consumption breakdowns in the benchmark output and a cost model. we can provide price estimates for hosted and dedicated variants.
[06:40] Aisha: timeline? what do you need to start?
[06:44] Samira: ideally traffic export + sample prompts + security answers. then Redwood spins up a test harness and runs two benchmark passes: representative and stress. total time about 2 weeks to run and analyze if we get data this week; shorter if we parallelize.
[07:05] Jordan: proposed POC window: data handoff by 7/29, bench run 7/30-8/06, analysis and review 8/07-8/12, joint call 8/13. does that align?
[07:20] Aisha: that works for our product timeline.
[07:26] Evan: one note: for the bench runs we require audit logs to be retained and a signed DPA.
[07:33] Jordan: we'll circulate DPA and attach to the next steps.
[07:38] [08:00] Samira: technical specifics for the benchmark matrix: we propose measuring p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latencies, tokens/sec, throughput (requests/sec), GPU utilization for dedicated runs, and model output quality metrics. we'll also include cold-start impact on latency for rarely used model variants.
[08:22] Markus: how do you measure cold start? we have scaled down pools overnight.
[08:28] Samira: we'll simulate a warm pool vs cold pool by controlling idle GPU counts in the Dedicated run or by calling cold-start endpoints in Hosted to capture startup latencies.
[08:36] Liam: for caching, we should instrument prefix hit rate and its effect on tokens per request. we'll ask for a sample of prefix sizes in your session logs.
[08:48] Dana: regarding model variants, we currently run a distilled in-house variant and are evaluating larger open models for better quality; cost vs latency tradeoffs are key. we want Redwood's recommendation for quantization and batching knobs.
[09:02] Samira: we'll propose a candidate stack: a small low-latency model for recommendations (quantized int8 path) and a higher-capacity variant for summarization. we'll include recommended batch sizes and KV cache parameters.
[09:15] [10:00] Jordan: any blockers for you to share the traffic?
[10:06] Markus: legal needs to review the scrub process; we can provide anonymized logs but need a checklist.
[10:12] Evan: yes please send the scrub checklist. Also we prefer logs delivered via S3 with SSE-KMS.
[10:20] Jordan: will do.
[10:25] Samira: on benchmarking harness: we'll provide a harness repo with a traffic replayer, runbook, and metrics dashboard (Grafana). We'll also include an example workload template you can run locally to validate. The harness will allow replaying user session stickiness and prompt mixes.
[10:48] Aisha: in the long term we might want private deployment; for the POC we're open to Redwood Dedicated if isolation guarantees hold.
[10:58] Samira: understood — Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; Private/VPC has more ops footprint. For the POC we can run Dedicated in a reserved pool and show performance.
[11:10] [11:40] Dana: small question on randomness — if we run multiple passes with the same prompts how do you ensure variance from model sampling doesn't skew results?
[11:49] Samira: we'll fix seeds where possible, and for sampling-heavy flows we'll run multiple iterations and report confidence intervals for quality metrics.
[12:02] Markus: what's the expected GPU footprint for baseline? rough estimate?
[12:08] Samira: preliminary estimate: for the recommendation traffic on a quantized small model, one A100-like card might handle ~12k tokens/sec with efficient batching; but we prefer to size by measured QPS and token mix from your export. We'll include a sizing table in the benchmark plan.
[12:28] Jordan: note that these are preliminary math — exact numbers depend on model variant and sequence length distribution.
[12:36] [13:00] Aisha: on compliance can you list what logs you'll need and how long you retain them in the POC?
[13:08] Samira: short answer: we can limit retention to the POC window (30 days) and export them to your S3; audit logs can be included in the package. We'll include retention controls in the runbook.
[13:20] Evan: please send the retention window options clearly.
[13:23] Samira: will do.
[13:28] [14:00] Jordan: let's capture success criteria again: 1) recommendation p95 < 350ms baseline; 2) summarization p95 < 2.2s; 3) quality parity within 3% on eval set; 4) cost <= 75% of current infra; 5) no unacceptable compliance gaps. Anything to add?
[14:45] Dana: also include stability under promotion spikes — no more than 2x degradation in p95 during 60s spikes.
[14:53] Samira: we'll include spike resilience thresholds.
[15:00] [15:30] Liam: what about routing/fallbacks if model capacity is saturated? do you support graceful degraded variants?
[15:39] Samira: yes Redwood has model routing and fallback policies; we'll configure a cheaper variant as a fallback during overloads; we'll measure quality drop in those scenarios.
[15:50] Markus: can we simulate region-based fallback? some traffic comes from EU region.
[15:56] Samira: yes we can emulate multi-region latency and routing policies in the stress run. please annotate regional splits in the traffic export.
[16:05] [16:40] Jordan: ok last items - pricing expectations. we'll propose a simple committed pricing for Dedicated during the POC and a hosted per-token estimate for comparison.
[16:54] Aisha: sounds good. Please include token units per 100k requests as you mentioned.
[17:02] Samira: will include. Also we'll surface tokenization variance across different model vocabularies — sometimes token counts shift by 5-12% between models which affects cost.
[17:18] Dana: good point.
[17:22] [18:00] Jordan: recap of next steps: Redwood sends benchmark plan + harness repo + compliance pack; Pictor provides anonymized traffic export + eval prompts + security answers; schedule infra access; runbench and sync.
[18:34] Aisha: confirmed.
[18:38] Evan: we'll review DPA and get back to you.
[18:42] [19:10] Samira: any open technical questions we didn't cover?
[19:16] Dana: none from product.
[19:20] Markus: none.
[19:23] Jordan: great — we'll follow up in email with all artifacts and a calendar invite for the 8/13 review. thanks everyone.
[19:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: speaker overlap and filler words present, occasional mis-transcriptions of acronyms (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash), product names sometimes truncated.
questions: What exact fields are required in the traffic export?
Can Redwood run benchmarks inside our VPC or do you need dedicated infra?
How is prefix cache hit rate instrumented in the benchmark?
